goal: Benchmark OMX-assisted execution against a non-OMX baseline for migrating the settings panel renderer to a React-managed JSX or TSX implementation.

task_batch.title: Define the migration boundary for the settings panel React conversion
acceptance_criteria: Identify the current settings entry points and renderer ownership boundaries
Keep the same migration scope and stop condition in both branches
Avoid folding unrelated settings architecture changes into the benchmark
task_batch.notes: Use src/settings/settings.html, src/settings/renderer.js, and src/preload/settings-bridge.ts as the primary migration anchors.

task_batch.title: Add or tighten acceptance tests before implementation
acceptance_criteria: Introduce task-specific tests or harness checks before implementation starts
Preserve existing settings and preload bridge tests unless stricter replacements are added
Run the same verification commands in both branches
task_batch.notes: This is the TDD gate for the experiment.

task_batch.title: Convert the settings renderer to React-managed JSX or TSX
acceptance_criteria: The settings UI is rendered through React components rather than a monolithic ad hoc renderer script
Tabs general, agents, theme, and about still render and use the existing settings API contract
The settings window still loads from src/settings/settings.html
task_batch.notes: TSX is preferred if the branch introduces a maintained TypeScript UI surface.

task_batch.title: Keep behavior parity and verify the migrated panel
acceptance_criteria: No regression is introduced in settings bridge usage
Verification output is recorded into the result JSON files
task_batch.notes: Use the same KPI capture flow for baseline and OMX branches.

fairness_constraints: same model and reasoning configuration where possible
reporting_requirements: copy the benchmark summary into both PR descriptions
